To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

selective inhibition of protein kinase (PKC) has no effect on maximal intracellular Ca2+, but significantly increases the duration of the calcium signal and the thromoxane B2 (TB2) generation in platelets.
the PKC inhibitors Ro 31-7529 and Ro 31 8220 inhibit PAF-induced dense granule release and aggregation in human platelets.
selective inhibition of PKC with Ro 31- 7549/001 or Ro 31-82 20/002 dose-dependently inhibits PAF-induced dense granule release and aggregation but does not affect PAF-induced elevation of [Ca2+] i.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of PKC in PAF-induced platelet functional activation.
the role played by protein kinase C in PAF-induced platelet activation.
the role of protein kinase-C in platelet-activated factor induced platelet activation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
PAF-induced platelet activation is a multi-faceted event, involving the concerted action of several signal transduction pathways, including PKC.
the PKC pathway plays a dual role in PAF-induced platelet functional response.
the role of PKC in PAF-induced platelet functional response is not simple and straightforward.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the inhibition of PKC by the inhibitors Ro31-7549 and Ro31-8220, results in a significant prolongation of the duration of the [Ca2+]I and TxB2 responses, while the inhibition of PKCa results in a significant inhibition of dense-granule and aggregation responses.
PKC plays a dual role in PAF-stimulating platelet activation.
PKC is involved in the control of PAF-induced Ca2+ mobilization, dense-granule secretion, aggregation and TxB2 release.
The main takeaway from our work is that
PKC is not the sole mediator of PAF-induced platelet responses.
the inhibition of PKC can be a useful therapeutic strategy for treating PAF-induced thrombotic disorders.
the inhibition of PKC by Ro 31 compounds is not sufficient to block PAF-induced platelet activation.
